transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this cross-functional check to finalize the production and shipment plan for the customer order of 3,600 pump modules — 600 sterile and 3,000 standard. As you know, Assembly Cell 2 is down due to an electrical fault, so we're working with Cells 1 and 4 only, and the customer requires shipment in the upcoming Sunday-Monday window. Before I lock the schedule, I need input from each of you: process engineering on cell capabilities and cycle times for both module types, quality systems on any inspection or validation requirements especially for the sterile units, workforce coordination on staffing availability across the cells, and logistics on pickup and shipping cutoffs for the Sunday-Monday window. Let's go around the table — what do we each need to flag?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical constraint on Cell 4. My commissioning review, completed this morning, found that Cell 4's newly installed fixture requires exactly 2 hours of setup verification before use, and Cell 4 is approved for no more than 1,200 modules during this campaign. This note hasn't been entered into the production schedule yet, so Elena, please account for this before locking the plan.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical quality requirement from the customer control plan. I confirmed in the current customer control plan — received yesterday via the customer portal — that all 600 sterile-pump modules must run on Cell 1 and receive a 100 percent pressure test before packing. Cell 4 has no compatible pressure tester, so sterile modules cannot be processed there. Important caveat: the local work-order file still shows the ordinary inspection route, so anyone working from that file will not see this requirement. Elena, this must be accounted for before the schedule is locked.
